title: Reflection Nebula Bernes 149 in Dark Cloud Lupus 3
caption: The reflection nebula Bernes 149 in the dark cloud Lupus 3, imaged by the Dark Energy Camera on the Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope
celestial: HR 5999, HR 6000 · constellation Scorpius · about 600 light-years away (source figure)
credit: CTIO/NOIRLab/DOE/NSF/AURA/ T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage/NSF NOIRLab). Image Processing: D. de Martin & M. Zamani (NSF NOIRLab)

recognition.text: Official NSF NOIRLab / Gemini press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Two young, low-mass protostars, HR 5999 and HR 6000, light up nearby dust in this image, creating the reflection nebula Bernes 149. The scene lies about 600 light-years away.

The stars grew out of the dusty dark cloud Lupus 3, part of a bigger complex that holds as many as nine dark clouds. Dark clouds are dense pockets of cold gas and dust, and they look dark because their dust blocks the light of stars behind them.

A reflection nebula shines differently from glowing gas. Its dust produces no light of its own but scatters the light of nearby stars toward us, rather like fog around a streetlamp. Protostars are stars still in the process of forming, gathering material from their surroundings. The picture was taken with the Dark Energy Camera (DECam) on the NSF Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope through g, r and i filters.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (103.26 x 58.21 arcminutes) and distance (600 light years), the frame spans roughly 18 × 10 light-years. Its light set out about 600 years before reaching the telescope.
